facts.text: Morton was renamed in 1856 after Elizabeth Morton Taylor, the wife of settler Colonel Caleb W., following its early settlement around 1850.
The town’s founding followed the 1830 Treaty of Dancing Rabbit Creek, which opened former Choctaw lands to white settlers in central Mississippi.
A Southern Railroad of Mississippi line reached Morton in 1858, linking the town to broader markets and sparking early trade.
In the early 1900s, the Hall‑Legan Lumber Company employed nearly 800 residents, making lumber a cornerstone of Morton’s economy.
Today, Morton hosts one of the world’s largest broiler producers, Koch Foods, whose plant has shaped the town’s demographics and labor history.
Morton is surrounded by the Bienville National Forest, offering residents and visitors a lush natural backdrop right on the town’s edge.
